newsitem.title: FRANCE: French GAN/CIC saga political scoring -Socialists.
newsitem.headline: French GAN/CIC saga political scoring -Socialists.

text.p: France's opposition Socialist Party accused Prime Minister Alain Juppe's centre-right government on Wednesday of political score-settling in ousting the chairman of state-owned insurer GAN, Jean-Jacques Bonnaud.

It also opposed the privatisation of GAN's regional banking subsidiary CIC, which the government has said it is determined to carry out despite abandoning a sell-off tender last week after attracting just one suitor, BNP.
"This is political settling of scores, and undoubtedly a precursor to a takeover of some other kind with other bosses in charge of privatising," the Socialist Party said.
"The Socialist Party deems the privatisation inappropriate," it said in a statement, adding that it wanted the GAN/CIC group held together.
"The government of Mr Alain Juppe has yet again demonstrated its mismanagement of privatisations," the statement said.

"The government weighed up the failure of its actions and backed off (on the CIC sale). It is now taking disciplinary action and calling for the resignation of GAN chairman Mr Jean-Jacques Bonnaud, and in the same blow the departure of CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt as well," it said.

Bonnaud is refusing to meet government calls for him to quit and stands to be fired by government decree next week. His successor would have the power to name a new chairman at GAN's CIC subsidiary, which government sources say would happen.
